newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases ahead of weekend.

text.p: After moving in leaps during the week, the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index eased 1.13 points on Friday to 3,233.75, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 10.640 million shillings traded on 370,385 shares from 30.354 million shillings traded on 798,034 shares, according to brokers and bourse officials.
A bourse official said despite the low volumes traded which were characteristic of a Friday when most players prepare for the weekend, price movement in the market was still impressive.

"There is a wind blowing across the market. I think the market is getting back on it's own two feet," a senior broker said. "The market is getting its break from new offers, financials and foreign demand," he added.
One broker said investors had taken positions early especially for the financials in anticipation of good end-year results.

The market has also seen a steady upward movement of prices in shares issued last year. Rea Vipingo traded at 10.50 from 10.05, while Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 80 from 85. Kenya Airways 9.50 from 9.25.
Brokers said there was increased demand from local investors who were buying those shares which hold a lot of foreign interest to sell later to foreign investors.
Power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co, whose price increase has been sustained by heavy foreign interest, eased a shilling to 165.

Some brokers said that recent announcements by the company of plans to expand and restructure had sparked off interest because it meant a bigger capitalisation. The firm is currently capitalised at 2.461 billion shillings.
Among commercials, Uchumi Supermarket gained 50 cents to close at 55 while Nation Printers & Publishers was unchanged at 110.
